definition: The MoE distinction between parameters used per token (active) and parameters stored overall (total).
details: The MoE distinction between parameters used per token (active) and parameters stored overall (total). "A 671B model with 37B active" means inference costs scale with 37B while capacity reflects 671B.

explainer.lead: Active and total parameters are two ways to measure a mixture-of-experts model. Active parameters are used for each token, while total parameters include everything the model stores, so the two counts describe different costs and capacity.

tiers.eli5: Imagine a huge library of specialists, but only a few are called to answer each question. The specialists answering are like active parameters, while everyone in the library makes up the total parameters. This lets the library hold a lot of knowledge without asking everyone to work on every question.
tiers.practitioner: For an MoE model, report both counts: use active parameters when describing per-token inference cost and total parameters when describing stored capacity. Do not compare models using one count as though it were the other; “671B total, 37B active” means inference scales with 37B while capacity reflects 671B.
tiers.paperLevel: Let P_total be all parameters stored by the model and P_active(t) be the parameters used to process token t. In an MoE model, these counts differ because only part of the model is active per token. Thus P_active(t) characterizes the per-token inference scale, while P_total characterizes overall capacity.

explainer.example: A model described as “671B with 37B active” stores 671B parameters overall. For each token, 37B parameters are active, so inference costs scale with 37B while the model’s capacity reflects 671B.

usedIn.name: Mixture-of-experts inference
usedIn.detail: Active parameters indicate the scale of computation used for each token.

usedIn.name: Model capacity reporting
usedIn.detail: Total parameters indicate how many parameters the model stores overall.

explainer.intuition: An MoE model is like a large team whose members are not all called in for every task. The whole team represents total capacity, while the members working on the current token represent the active portion.
howItWorks: Store the model’s complete collection of parameters; this is the total count.
For each token, use only the portion selected by the MoE mechanism.
Count that per-token portion as the active parameters.
Interpret inference cost using the active count and model capacity using the total count.
explainer.whyItMatters: The distinction prevents a large stored model from being mistaken for one that uses all its parameters on every token. It gives separate, clearer measures of per-token inference cost and overall capacity.
misconceptions: Total parameters are not all necessarily used for each token.
Active parameters do not measure the model’s full stored capacity.
“37B active” does not mean the model stores only 37B parameters.
